# Child Activation Functions

A Compute Definition that prepares child documents with independently declared parties and explicit identity mappings, while retaining legacy construction using parent role names. It also inherits activation, access, party-management and amendment helpers.

The child-preparation functions return a document value. They do not initialize the child, record consent, grant timeline permissions or establish that it is active. Document reads refer to the document executing the helper—the configuring parent during preparation. Child paths refer to the supplied `child` value.

## Explicit child preparation

`prepareChild(child, mapping, suppliedRoles)` defaults `child` and `mapping` to `{}` and `suppliedRoles` to `[]`. It rejects a child containing `/contracts/initialized` with `CHILD_ALREADY_INITIALIZED`, and requires the exact Activation Clause at `/clauses/activation/type`, otherwise `CHILD_ACTIVATION_REQUIRED`.

Party declarations come from the child’s `/clauses/activation/parameters/parties`; configuring parties come from the executing document’s `/activation/parties`. Both must be nonempty objects, and `mapping` must be an object.

- Each `mapping` key names a declared child role. Its value is either a configuring-party role name or an explicit Party. There is no automatic mapping by matching role names.
- Every child role needs a mapping unless listed in `suppliedRoles`. A supplied role must be declared and unmapped; its declaration is retained unchanged, potentially awaiting later resolution.
- Child role names must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`.
- Mapped Parties require `lead/channel` and a nonempty `readerKeys` list containing unique, nonempty strings. Each is checked as a specialization of its child declaration.
- Every configuring party must remain represented in the resulting roster by the same lead channel and the same reader-key set, regardless of key order. Names, business descriptions and additional representatives do not establish this main identity. Child role names may differ, and additional valid mapped parties are permitted.

`bindChild(child, mapping)` delegates to `prepareChild` with `suppliedRoles: []`, requiring mappings for every child declaration.

Preparation replaces the child’s declared `parties` with the resolved roster and preserves its other activation parameters. Existing child `accessPaths` default to `[]`. Each configuring-document access path adds a reference under `/timelineAccess/configurerN`, numbered from the current child access-path count, and appends that child path. An occupied target rejects with `CHILD_ACCESS_PATH_CONFLICT`.

For roster entries containing `lead/channel`, preparation installs lead transports at `/contracts/<role>` and representative transports at `/contracts/<role>__<repId>`. An identical existing transport is accepted; a different existing value rejects with `CHILD_CHANNEL_CONFLICT`. Retained declarations without a lead channel do not produce transports.

## Legacy child construction

`activateChild(child, frozen, readerNames, roles)` defaults `child` to `{}` and both lists to `[]`; no default is specified for the Boolean `frozen`. If the executing document has no `/activation`, it returns `child` unchanged.

Otherwise, empty `roles` selects all parent parties. Explicit roles must exist in `/activation/parties`, and every requested reader name must exist in `/activation/readers`; failures are `CHILD_PARTY_NOT_IN_PARENT` and `CHILD_READER_NOT_IN_PARENT`. Empty `readerNames` selects no additional reader groups.

This function replaces the child’s `timelineAccess` with references named `grant0`, `grant1`, and so on, taken from the parent’s `/activation/accessPaths`. It replaces `/clauses/activation` with an Activation Clause, retaining existing parameters except for the newly supplied `parties`, `readers`, `accessPaths` and `frozen`. The child’s existing `required` list is retained, defaulting to `[]`; it is not copied from the parent. Lead and representative transports are written into `/contracts`, overwriting matching entries. This legacy function does not perform the initialization or collision checks of `prepareChild`.

## Inherited access and activation

`transports` derives lead and representative channels from a roster. `readerGroups` combines additional `readers` with party `readerKeys` and representative `readerKeys`, using role names and `<role>__<repId>` names; roster-derived groups replace additional groups with matching names.

`accessValid` reads access documents at its `accessPaths`; `accessRecordsValid` checks supplied documents directly. Every non-External transport must be a Timeline Channel. For each such transport, one Timeline Access document must match its exact timeline and provider and contain at least one allowed key from **every** reader group. Keys within a group are alternatives; an empty group cannot satisfy this check. External Channel transports are exempt. Access coverage and operation authority remain separate checks.

`computeState` derives `/activation` status from the roster, access evidence, approvals and agreed terms. Pending `accessRequests` whose `expectedRevision` matches the current `revision` also contribute parties to the access check.

- `functional` and `accessReady` report access validity.
- `termsAccepted` requires approval for every role in `required` and unchanged values at the paths recorded in `terms/fields`. Missing approval entries are treated as false by this check; missing `required` and `terms/fields` use empty collections.
- `active` requires access readiness, accepted current terms and a document that is not `closed`.
- `status` is `CLOSED` first; otherwise missing access produces `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` or, after earlier activation, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`. With access, it is `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` or `ACTIVE`.
- `reason` reports `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` or an empty string. An empty reason alone does not establish activity, because closure is handled separately.

`commitState` persists changed activation state and maintains `everActivated`. It emits Document Activated on first activation, Document Access Suspended when an active document loses access, and Document Access Restored when activity resumes after access was unavailable. Initial party channels remain empty Composite External Channels until access is ready; conflicting unrelated contracts reject installation.

`requireActive` checks stored `active` and current access, additionally checking current role or representative membership when `workflow` is true. `businessReady` checks closure, required approvals, current terms and access. Both deliberately return true when `/activation` is absent; that fallback is not evidence that a child was activated.

## Acceptance, party changes and admissions

`approve` and `approveWithTerms` require `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be true, `call/channel` to name a party lead, `input.revision` to match `/activation/revision`, and valid participant access. When `negotiation/allowedPaths` is nonempty, `termsRef` must be text; any supplied `termsRef` must match `/activation/terms/ref`. Repeated approval returns true without another acceptance event. New approval records the party’s acceptance, commits state and emits Terms Accepted. A true return records successful acceptance, not necessarily activation. If the resulting state is active, negotiation becomes uneditable and a pending negotiation proposal is marked `SUPERSEDED`.

`updatePartyPublic` delegates to `updateParty` after removing the input’s type annotation. Updates require exact-document review and an unfrozen roster. Only a party lead may manage its own existing party. `input.party` defaults to the invoking role; adding a new role requires an explicit key and `allowNewParties`. The replacement must contain `lead/channel`, representative names must satisfy the same naming restrictions as party roles, and the resulting roster must pass access checks. Successful updates install roster channels and approval/update handlers, clear approvals, increment `revision`, add newly created roles to `required`, and emit Party Changed. No input revision is required. Missing `frozen` and `allowNewParties` are treated as false by these guards.

`requestPartyAddition` reads the current event, ignores stale `expectedRevision` values and repeated `admissionRef` values, validates supplied `accessDocuments`, and records pending additions in `/activation/accessRequests`. Existing parties lacking the required sharing receive Party Access Update Requested events. These events request access changes; they do not change provider permissions or admit participants. `refreshAccessRequests` updates readiness from available evidence for requests matching the current revision.

`admitApprovedParties` requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, nonempty configured `admission/approvers`, valid main identities and sufficient access. Its body checks that an admission policy exists; it does not itself collect or verify approver votes. Existing roles must retain their main identity and are not replaced. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; otherwise it installs roster contracts, increments `revision`, commits state and emits Party Changed events carrying `admissionRef`. It does not automatically add admitted roles to `required`.

## Terms, amendments and access histories

`initializeTerms` returns existing terms unchanged. Otherwise it derives them from `/clauseRuntime/initialDocument`, separating the existing scalar fields named by `negotiation/allowedPaths` and excluding referenced access documents, activation `accessPaths` and `readers`, and party-level `readerKeys`. Missing or nonscalar negotiation fields reject initialization. It starts `termsRevision` and negotiation `revision` at 1, with editing enabled and empty proposal/history collections. `refresh` initializes missing terms, commits activation state and refreshes access-request readiness.

When parties or required approvers change after terms exist, `commitState` updates the terms reference and increments `termsRevision`. It clears approvals when negotiable paths are configured and invalidates a pending negotiation proposal with `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`.

The inherited `recordAmendmentProposal` and `approveAmendmentProposal` use their supplied `bindings.state` and `bindings.editable` document paths. Proposals require matching `expectedRevision`, a path listed in `parameters.paths`, editable state equal to true, and a nonempty `proposalId` without `/` or `~`. Exact pending retries return `duplicate`; conflicting or previously used identifiers reject. `preservePending` defaults to false; true prevents replacing a different pending proposal. Recording emits Amendment Proposed without applying the replacement.

Amendment approval requires `call/channel` in `parameters.approvers`. Applied proposals and repeated approvals return `duplicate`; other approvals require the current proposal identifier and editable state. Only after every configured approver accepts does the helper replace the target field, record history, increment the amendment revision, clear the proposal and emit Amendment Applied. `acceptedNew` can therefore mean an approval was recorded while the amendment remains pending.

`installTimelineAccess` accepts 1–16 `input.documents` and an `input.basePath`. It validates Timeline Access type, public provider channel, initialization and provider checkpoint history, and the prescribed provider/update contract structure. It deduplicates by original document identity, embeds new references, appends activation access paths and registers update-driven refresh handlers. It returns `duplicate` when nothing is added or `acceptedNew` when new histories are installed. Installation does not modify their permission sets; permission updates remain provider-owned. `requirePartyAccessDocuments` additionally checks supplied transport names, nonempty transport reader groups, and matching timelines/providers; actual reader-key coverage is checked separately by the access-validity helpers.
